# 08-fresco — sources

Back-test entry `08-fresco.yaml`: Fresco, the AI scribe for construction superintendents (YC Fall 2024).
Written 2026-10-22 from public material only. Quotes are verbatim from the page named; "Author's choice" marks the
smallest plausible choice made where the public material is silent.

Main sources:
- [HN] Launch HN: Fresco (YC F24), 2024-11-21 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42204939
- [LYC] Launch YC: Fresco, the scribe for construction, 2024-10-23 — https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/M73-fresco-the-scribe-for-construction
- [YCP] YC company page — https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fresco (now "AI-powered takeoff and estimating for Division 8 construction")
- [KOE] A contractor's daily-log expectations on Procore's support site — https://support.procore.com/tc/Koester/Site_Map/Koester_Expectations_-_Daily_Logs
- [SWI] Swiftask, Procore daily reports page (vendor) — https://swiftask.ai/ai-integration/procore/intelligent-daily-reports
- [BLS] BLS Occupational Outlook, construction managers — https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/construction-managers.htm
- [OPU] Launch HN: Opusense (field reports for site inspectors), 2025-05-20 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44042791

## The eight founder-emulation items

1. **Who.** Construction superintendents on commercial jobs.
   [HN] "Superintendents are the busiest and most expensive people on construction sites."
   [LYC] "That’s the reality for 210k+ construction superintendents (or supervisors, foremen, PMs, etc.) across the USA."
   → `roles[superintendent]`, `context.actor`, `actor_plural`. Author's choice: "on commercial jobs" (the founders ask
   for introductions to commercial general contractors in [LYC]).

2. **What (the job).** Keep the record of the day's work, for liability and disputes.
   [HN] "30-200 photos per day to document site progress (mostly for liability reasons, or in case of a dispute with the
   owner over delays and deliverables)"; photos used to create "daily logs", "structured documents that account for the
   work done on site on any given day". [KOE] the log is "a critical piece of documentation in the arbitration of a
   dispute". → `statements.problem`, `context.job`, `interpretations.problem`.

3. **When / where.** At the end of the day, after the site walks, in the trailer.
   [HN] "At the end of the day, they'll spend a few hours uploading those photos into OneDrive, or project management
   software like Procore or ACC." [YCP] "We were curious what superintendents were doing for hours in their trailers at
   the end of the day." [LYC] "supes are spending up to 3 hours a day creating documents". → `context.circumstance`, `occasion: daily log`.
   Author's choice: the recall window {5, WORKING_DAYS} and Frequency 4 to 5 working days out of 5 (the posts say "per
   day"; a five-day site week is assumed). Prevalence `p_80_100` ("Nearly all") follows from the same "per day".

4. **Which people (the comparable group).** Superintendents at US general contractors whose jobs run on Procore or ACC.
   [LYC] "210k+ construction superintendents ... across the USA"; "Project management tools like Procore and ACC have
   dramatically increased documentation requirements". [YCP] "driving to Napa, South Bay, and around SF". → `context.segment`,
   `market: US`.

5. **Who pays.** The general contractor, per site.
   [HN] "we charge per site per month, which includes unlimited users on any given construction project".
   → `persona.decision_maker: {role: contractor}`, the BUYER role. Author's choice: the decider is the contractor's
   "operations lead" and the role to test is "The CFO" (a second role, "The project executive", listed); Purchase
   friction's three steps ("A trial on one live job" tested, a Procore check, a security review) and Commitment's step
   "start a paid pilot on one site" are the author's. Public material names no buyer title; [LYC] asks for
   introductions to general contractors by firm, not by role.

6. **Mechanism.** Narrated short videos turned into notes, texted to the crew, pushed to Procore/ACC.
   [HN] "Supers simply take short videos with voiceover, or upload photos, and Fresco does the rest, creating notes with
   transcription, photos, assignees, and due dates. Supers can easily text their crew action items, and receive texts
   back". "We also route this to whatever project management software they're using with a single click."
   [LYC] the narrated example "The beam in the southwest corner of room 134 is corroded and needs replacement by Alex.";
   "Supes who use Fresco complete their notes, on average, 90% faster."
   → `statements.solution`, `solution_mechanism`, Compatibility and Adoption friction items. Relative advantage's two
   benefits are from [HN] ("during their site walks, not after") and [LYC] ("90% faster"); their wording is the author's.

7. **Price.** About $1k per site per month, less with multi-site or multi-month terms.
   [HN] "The typical price is $1k/month, but we offer discounts for multi-month or multi-site commitments."
   → `commercial.price` {800, 1000, month}. Author's choice: the low end of $800 stands for the stated discounts.
   Existing sacrifice: 30 to 60 hours a month per site at an hourly rate of 55 — from [LYC] "up to 3 hours a day" and
   [HN] "a few hours uploading", taken as 1.5 to 3 hours on about twenty working days (author's arithmetic). The rate is
   [BLS] "$55.28 per hour" (median, construction managers, May 2025), the author's stand-in: no superintendent wage is
   in the public material. Ability to pay is derived by code (24% to 61%).

8. **Occasions.** The narrated beam; a school refit report; the uploads and logs at the end of the day.
   [LYC] on a school refit walkthrough: "Normally, creating the final report takes 2+ hours."
   [HN] "few supers have time to do this thoroughly, so these photos aren't very searchable." No named customer quote
   exists in public; the occasions below are scripted from these and from practitioner comments.

No respondent carries the name of a commenter, customer or founder.

## Open
- The verdict was scripted to be plausible and not obviously "build": the problem holds on how often but people
  disagree on whether the log is one of their two worst difficulties; the solution splits on the benefit and on
  talking over videos on site; the price fails (two of eight at the founder's band or above) while the cost it would
  replace is above the price. This is the author's reading of the thread's sceptics, not a measured result.
- No public account names a buyer title at a general contractor; the decider, the tested role "The CFO", the purchase
  steps and the Commitment step are the author's.
- hourly_rate 55 is a proxy (construction managers, not superintendents).
- Existing sacrifice picks use `period: quarter` (the corpus's convention), although the registry's recall period for a
  monthly cost reads "last month"; the values are the monthly figures times three.
- The window {5, WORKING_DAYS} is the author's; the public posts say "per day".

insights.line: What made the others more pressing?

whys.g1: Both answers are about subs not showing and the schedule slipping, so one group named plainly for keeping the schedule and getting subs to show is exactly how a super would sort them.
whys.g2: There is no junk, explicit or off-topic answer on this line, so nothing junk was grouped.

founder.order_why: It runs from naming and market, through the context and recall window, to how common and how often the daily log is, what else is hard and today's workaround, and then the sending, which is how I'd explain my problem to a stranger.
founder.asked_twice: Screens 3 and 5 ask the same question ('Before we test anything, let's define exactly where this idea applies.'), with the recall window between them, so the context step reads as if it is asked twice.
founder.missing: Nothing asks about the solution (short narrated videos and photos turned into notes, texted to the crew and pushed to Procore or ACC), the price (about $1k per site per month, less for multi-site or multi-month terms), or who pays (the general contractor per site, not the superintendent who does the log). Screens 8 and 9 also say 'typed the day's notes', but my supers mostly upload 30-200 photos and write them up, so no screen asks about the photo upload and sorting that takes their hours.

PRIMARY.order_why: It goes from whether my jobs run on Procore or ACC, to whether and how often I typed up the log, to what I'd want easier, to how the last log went, which is how I'd tell it, though screens 1 and 2 both say '1 of 4'.
PRIMARY.asked_twice: Screens 2 and 3 overlap: if I typed the notes on some days, the 'how many days' question already covers the yes/no.
PRIMARY.missing: Nothing about the photos, which are the slow part for me: getting the day's site-walk pictures uploaded and attached to the log takes hours. Also nothing on how long the log took, or whether I've had to pull old logs to back up a delay dispute with the owner.

screens.why1: Choosing who reads my questions to supers belongs here, after the questions are written and just before the link goes out by text.
screens.why2: The question reads cleanly, but the hint says the interviewer is on video and then talks only about the voice I record, so I'm not sure whether I'm picking a face, a voice or both.
screens.why3: I can play each 5-second clip and judge which one a superintendent in the trailer would sit through, so this is mine to answer.
screens.why4: Two named interviewers, each with a preview, and the default already marked; nothing is missing or doubled.
screens.why5: It says construction superintendents as I typed it, and nothing about Fresco, the contractor buyer or the price shows on this screen.
screens.instead: Who should ask construction superintendents your questions on video? Each option shows her face and plays her voice. Daphne ▶ (picked for you) · Saskia ▶

screens.why1: Once I've picked who asks, the next obvious choice before sending is how my supers will answer, so this belongs right before the link goes out.
screens.why2: Mostly plain, but 'they pick Daphne or text' trips me, because to a super 'text' means texting the crew from the truck, not the read-and-tap version of the questions.
screens.why3: I know my supers answer from the trailer or the truck between walks, often with gloves off and noise around, so I can judge whether talking on video or tapping suits them.
screens.why4: The three ways (talk to Daphne, read and tap, or let them choose) are distinct and cover the real choice, and no escape is needed for a founder's setting.
screens.why5: My pick, 'Read and tap', is offered as I chose it, and nothing of Fresco or my buyer roles shows to the respondent.
screens.instead: Keep it, but change the third option to 'Both are offered; they pick Daphne or reading and tapping when they open the link.'

screens.why1: Right after choosing how supers answer, it's obvious I now pick who gets the links before sending.
screens.why2: Mostly plain, but 'the Contacts page' and 'signs in with Google' are Keel's own terms I only half know at this point, and the first option's tail 'I send each one their own link' reads like a second label rather than a description.
screens.why3: I know whether I'm texting supers I've met on site walks or posting in a group, so this is mine to answer.
screens.why4: The three routes are distinct and cover how I'd reach supers, but the options mix voices ('I send' vs 'you send') and there's no route for introductions through a GC contact, which is how I actually reach supers.
screens.why5: My pick, people I know by name, is kept, and nothing of Fresco's product or roles leaks to a respondent here.
screens.instead: Who gets a link? -- Supers I know by name (I send each their own link) / Supers from a Keel contact list (Keel makes a link each, I send them) / A group or forum where supers already are (one open link, each signs in with Google)

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits under the title with '4 counted', but '5 needed' only appears down on the cards, and naming Frequency alone is confusing when Importance and Current solution are short by the same one person.
screens.why_b2: There is no chart here, and the tally '1 holding · 3 too few to call · 7 people answered' is plain, but the kicker's '4 TO 7 COUNTED' and Prevalence's 'bar 6 of 7 · at the bar' (my 8 in 10 turned into a count) took me a second look.
screens.why_b3: The statement, Prevalence and Frequency are my words, but Importance is rewritten into an awkward 'five things that are hard... one of the two', and Current solution's 'still falls short' is recognisable though not how I'd say it.
screens.why_b4: Nothing tells me what to do: not whether I need one more superintendent to answer, why three of my seven weren't counted, or whether I can move on to the solution with only Prevalence holding.
screens.why_b5: The 7 who answered and the 4 counted stay in view, three beliefs are honestly called too few to call, and Prevalence holding at exactly the bar is not dressed up as strong.
screens.instead: Too few to call: three of my four beliefs have 4 counted where 5 are needed; get one more superintendent who walked a site this week (3 of 7 weren't counted, say why) before reading Frequency, Importance and Current solution, and only Prevalence holds so far, 6 of 7, right at the bar.

screens.why_b1: The status 'Holding up' sits right beside '6 of 7 said yes · bar 6 of 7 · at the bar', so I see both the verdict and the number that decides it.
screens.why_b2: The strip shows 6 cells for and 1 against on a 0-to-7 axis, with my bar marked at 6, so what is counted, out of how many, and where the bar sits are plain at first look.
screens.why_b3: I recognise the belief, but the line drops 'on commercial jobs' and 'after the site walks'. 'Typed the day's notes into the daily log' is what every super does, not the hours of typing in the trailer after the walk that I counted.
screens.why_b4: 'How often, and whether it matters, are the next two cards' sends me onward, but it doesn't say what clearing the bar by the minimum, with 7 people, means for Fresco.
screens.why_b5: The low n is said ('a lean, not a call'). But 'Holding up' and 'Common among these 7' lean on a gate that a super who logs as she goes, like Denise, also answers Yes to, and the stage page I just read said 'Too few to call'.
screens.instead: At your bar exactly: 6 of 7 supers typed up the daily log after their walks in the last 5 working days. Seven people is a lean, not a call, and one more No would drop it below your 8 in 10.

screens.why_b1: The status 'Too few to call' sits right beside '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', and the So line repeats the same number, so I know why there is no verdict yet.
screens.why_b2: I can find the median at 5 and the four filled cells against the bar, but the axis starts at a 0 nobody could pick, and the legend 'what you said · at what you said · short of it' takes a second look to map onto the cells.
screens.why_b3: Frequency and my 4 to 5 working days out of 5 are mine, but 'type the day's notes into the daily log' is code's clause, not how I put it (photos and notes going into the log after the walks), and 'Asked: Asked:' is printed twice.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic: it does not tell me that all four counted answers are at 4 or 5, or that one more counted superintendent would settle it.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible, the two uncounted people are named with their reasons, and the small group is called 'a lean, not a call'; the only slip is '— the most recent time it happened' tagged onto a five-day count question, which is a mislabel rather than a claim the data cannot carry.
screens.instead: Too few to call: all 4 counted supers logged on 4 or 5 of the last 5 working days (middle answer 5); one more counted answer decides it, so get the next superintendent before reading this as a pattern.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits right beside its deciding number, '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', and the So line repeats both.
screens.why_b2: The caption makes plain that the bars count 8 picks from 4 people, but the bar reads '4 of 5' next to '4 counted' and is drawn only on the strip, not on the chart, so I had to look twice to see that 4 of 5 is two-thirds of the floor.
screens.why_b3: The card is titled Importance, and the belief line uses my five rows with my own item 'Getting photos and notes logged' as the one tested.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' does not tell me to get one more counted answer, and it does not point at the split where scheduling and subs drew three picks each against my two.
screens.why_b5: 'A small group: a lean, not a call' suggests a lean when the count is 2 for and 2 against, which leans nowhere.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 2 of 4 put photos and notes in their two, 2 picked planning and subs instead; one more counted answer decides it, and the bar is 4 of 5.

screens.why_b1: 'Too few to call' sits right beside '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', so I know the verdict and the number behind it.
screens.why_b2: The rung counts and the line under 'Done in the trailer in under an hour' read at once, but the strip's 'your bar · 4 of 5' with only 4 counted and a ghost cell took me a second look to work out what the marker means.
screens.why_b3: Current solution is mine, but 'typing up the daily log in the trailer' is Keel's rewording of getting the day's photos and notes into the log, and it puts the act in the trailer when my own top rung, which Denise picked, is 'Done on site'.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic; it doesn't say that 3 of the 4 counted already land below my line, or that one more counted answer decides it.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible, the two people not counted are named with reasons, and it says 'a small group: a lean, not a call' instead of claiming the belief held.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 3 of the 4 counted took a couple of hours or more after the walk. One more counted answer decides it, and 4 of 5 would hold, so get Hank or Luis, or one more super, to answer from their last log.

screens.why_b1: The status 'Too few to call' sits beside '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', so I know there is no verdict and why, but the screen never says how the 4 split on my belief: '2 against' shows, while the other two are only implied to be for it.
screens.why_b3: Importance and the belief line, with the circumstance about photos and notes going into the daily log, are the ones I checked on the way in, in my own words.
screens.why_b4: '5 needed to call it' implies I need more answers, but the screen never says to get more superintendents, or what the schedule-and-subs theme means for pitching Fresco as a log tool.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible everywhere (4 counted, 2 against, a group of 2), the low n is named as too few to call, and no claim goes beyond the two who answered the why.
screens.why_b6: I did not type that a super who logs on the tablet before leaving the gate rates it low, or that 'the log can wait till morning, the deck can't', and both tell me the log loses to tomorrow's subs and crane whenever the day goes wrong, which bears on how I position Fresco.
screens.instead: Say '2 for · 2 against of 4, too few to call; the 2 against put tomorrow's schedule and subs first, so ask more supers and test pitching the log as freeing time for tomorrow's plan.'

screens.why1: As the first screen it's obvious they're checking I'm the kind of super they want before asking about my logs, and it doesn't repeat anything.
screens.why2: Procore and ACC are the platforms every GC super I know works in, so I read and answer it in one go.
screens.why3: I know which platform each of my jobs runs on, so I answer from fact, not a guess.
screens.why4: Yes or No covers it for a gate, and 'any of the jobs' means a super on a mixed setup still has a true answer; no escape is right since the gate has none.
screens.why5: It keeps the founder's segment, jobs on Procore or ACC, without telling me anything about a product or what they're building.
screens.why6: Short and one question, but 'ACC' is said as three letters a listener might not catch as Autodesk Construction Cloud, and 'I'll read 2 options' before 'Yes; or No' is clunkier than just 'Yes or no.' as the screener's spoken form says.
screens.instead: Do any of the jobs you run now use Procore or Autodesk Construction Cloud? Yes or no.

screens.why1: Right after asking whether my jobs run on Procore or ACC, asking about my daily log in the last week is the obvious next step.
screens.why2: Typing the day's notes into the daily log is exactly how I'd say it, and I can answer on first read.
screens.why3: I do the daily log every working day, so I know straight away whether I typed notes into it this week.
screens.why4: Yes and No cover it cleanly, and the chips belong to the story box after a Yes, not to this gate.
screens.why5: Nothing of the product leaks, but dropping 'after your site walks' turns the founder's problem (typing it all up later) into the plain routine, so the meaning has drifted.
screens.why6: One short question with 'Yes or no' is easy to hear once and answer.
screens.why7: The gate asks about the circumstance every superintendent is in, since we all put the day's notes into the log, so nearly everyone says Yes and No has almost no one: the belief can't be refuted, which is the card's bad case.
screens.instead: In the last 5 working days, did you type up the daily log after your site walks? Yes · No

screens.why1: Right after I said yes to typing the day's notes into the daily log, asking how many of the last five days I did it is the obvious next question.
screens.why2: Daily log, the day's notes, working days: that's how I talk about my day, and I can answer on one hearing.
screens.why3: I know exactly which days this week I sat down at the end of the day and typed the log, so I can answer without guessing.
screens.why4: One through five covers every working day after a yes, the counts don't overlap, and 'I can't recall' is the right way out; though most supers will hit 5 because the log is owed every day the job runs.
screens.why5: It asks the same act as the screen before, the notes into the daily log, and nothing about anybody's product or plan reaches me.
screens.why6: Heard once it's short and one question, 'a number from 1 to 5' is easy to hold, and the escape is said last and short.
screens.why7: Every option counts days of the window from 1 to 5, the last is the window's count, there's no 0, and 'I can't recall' sits apart; whether a count can go against depends on a founder's low I wasn't shown.

screens.why1: Right after asking how many days I typed up the log, asking what part of my day I'd most want easier makes obvious sense.
screens.why2: Subs, RFIs, submittals, crews, the walk, the log: that's how I talk on a GC job, and I can answer on first hearing.
screens.why3: Every one of these is on my plate at the end of a day on site, so I can pick from what I actually did yesterday.
screens.why4: 'Planning tomorrow's work and crews' and 'Lining up subs to show up tomorrow' overlap for me, since my subs are most of my crews; 'Chasing RFIs and submittals' is two things in one row and partly my PM's or PE's chase.
screens.why5: Nothing of the product leaks, but 'getting photos and notes logged' reads as the upload chore rather than keeping an accurate record of the day, so it drifts a little from the founder's words.
screens.why6: Short stem, five short options I can hold, and one escape said last; it says well.
screens.why7: The own item is there, not first, with three-plus rivals and None of these at the first ask, so the belief can be supported or refuted; but two rivals overlap (tomorrow's crews vs. subs), one row holds two things (RFIs and submittals), and the own row leans toward restating the circumstance rather than the record kept.
screens.instead: Think of your last working day on site. Which one of these would you most like made easier? Planning tomorrow's work and crews · Following up on safety issues from the walk · Chasing open RFIs · Keeping an accurate record of the day in the log · None of these

screens.why1: After asking which part of the day I'd most like made easier, asking how my last log went is the obvious next question.
screens.why2: Daily log, the walk, the trailer: that's how we talk on a job, and I get it on one read.
screens.why3: I write the log every day, so I know exactly how long my last one took and where I did it.
screens.why4: The stem says the log was typed in the trailer, but the first option says it was done on site, so they clash; and on a lot of jobs my assistant super or the PE writes the log, which no option or chip covers.
screens.why5: Putting 'in the trailer' into the stem adds a method the founder never asked about; their concern is getting the walk's photos and notes into the log, not where it gets typed.
screens.why6: One short question and five short options I can hold in my head, though 'daily log' said twice in a row is clunky.
screens.why7: The rungs are all time, run best to worst, have two working rungs above a line after 2, and end with it never getting done, but the escape is 'I can't recall' when the card wants 'Someone else did it' for a log that can be handed off.
screens.instead: Think of your last daily log. How did getting the day's photos and notes into it go? Done during the walk, nothing left after; Done in under an hour after the walk; Took a couple of hours after the walk; Took the rest of the evening; Never got written up that day; or Someone else did it.
